text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
AL-AHRAM

- Mubarak says Egypt wants the peace process to continue and that Egypt has no interest in Sudan's instability. He says while visiting site of New Valley Canal that development is progressing in Egypt according to set plans with the purpose of making the best use of resources for the sake of the people.
- Suzanne Mubarak heads Unesco committee meeting to select best children's book.
- Mubarak says while flying over Sharm el-Sheikh that new projects will not be a financial burdern on coming generations. Ministerial committee to oversee land use in Gulf of Aqaba.
- Mubarak to hold talks with Jacques Chriac in Paris on Friday.
- Mubarak tells New York Times in an interview that the Egyptian public would not accept his visit to Israel until the Jewish state changed its policies.
- Mubarak to signal start of use of new national identification cards.
- Very positive talks between Arafat and Clinton; U.S. president says settlements in Jerusalem will jolt confidence between the two sides.
AL-AKHBAR
- Mubarak tours Toshka project work site. He tells reporters that he will discuss Jerusalem with Netanyahu.
- Mubarak issues important decrees in Sharm el-Sheikh: orders building permits to be issued quickly and without obstacles in tourist sites.
- U.S. sources say Mubarak will present new ideas and suggestions on ways to resume peace process on all tracks during his visit to Washington.
- Sudanese opposition leader Mohammed Osman al-Mirghani praises President Mubarak's stance on Sudan; Mirghani met Agriculture Minister Youssef Wali.
- Foreign Minister Moussa says Egypt will support Arafat if he unilaterally declares Palestinian state.
- Egypt's Ahli wins Arab "Super" cup.
- Suspects in devil-worshipping case released.
AL-GOMHURIA
- Mubarak says will discuss Jerusalem and the danger of settlements with Netanyahu.
- Mubarak tells New York Times that settlement in Jerusalem could lead to bigger problem.
- Rain delays flights for 105 passengers.
- 15 education officials in Dimyatt embezzled three million pounds.
$1 = 3.395 pounds
